newsitem.title: USA: Rabbis charged with laundering drug money get bail.
newsitem.headline: Rabbis charged with laundering drug money get bail.

text.p: Two Orthodox Jewish rabbis indicted for allegedly laundering $750,000 in Colombian drug profits through a Brooklyn synagogue and yeshiva were freed Tuesday on bail.

Federal prosecutors allege the two men -- Rabbi Bernard Grunfeld, 64, president of Congregation Eitz Chaim and Bobover Yeshiva, and Mahir Reiss, 47, a rabbi and real estate manager -- were part of a 12-person ring charged with conspiring to launder drug money.

Grunfeld and Reiss were both released on a $750,000 bond each in Brooklyn Federal Court. Reiss' brother, Abraham, 48, also was named in the indictment and was freed Monday on $750,000 bond. The three face up to 20 years in prison if convicted of the charges.

The indictment alleged in part that the defendants wired $2.4 million out of a Swiss bank account to buy a Beech Super King airplane, a favourite of drug smugglers. The plane was delivered to suspected drug dealers in Colombia.
Susan Kellman, an attorney for the Reisses and Grunfeld, said the indictment was "filled with a variety of gross distortions."

The indictment alleged the three laundered the money through accounts of the Brooklyn synagogue and yeshiva, or Orthodox Jewish school. The synagogue's neighbourhood is the centre of the 40,000-member Orthodox Bobov sect.

The defendants were charged with laundering $750,000 in 1995 and 1996. They were also charged with violating federal financial reporting rules by moving $1 million in 95 separate transactions of less than $10,000 each. The number of transactions triggered the federal investigation.
Twelve defendants were named and three were still at large. Eight of those charged are Colombian nationals.
